ttl.name: How to Troubleshoot ECU Controlled Systems

atten4.ptxt: Perform troubleshooting in accordance with the diagnostic procedure below. Only the basic procedure is shown here. For details, the most effective method for each circuit is described in the section for each system. Before starting troubleshooting of the relevant circuit, check the troubleshooting procedure first.

descript-testgroup.testtitle: Customer Problem Analysis and Malfunction Analysis

test1.ptxt: Confirm with the customer the conditions and circumstances when the problem occurred, and fill out the customer problem analysis check sheet.

descript-testgroup.testtitle: Confirm Problem Symptom and Check DTCs (Including Freeze Frame Data)

test1.ptxt: Using SST (Toyota electrical tester), inspect the battery voltage.
Inspect areas that can be checked visually, such as blown fuses, open or short circuits in the wire harness and poor connector connections.
Confirm the problem location, symptom and conditions, and check the DTCs according to the relevant chart.

specitem.ptxt: To each Diagnostic Trouble Code Chart

test1.ptxt: Some systems lose their memory when the battery negative terminal is disconnected, and some systems return to the initial state when parts are replaced, so record the vehicle's settings before repair.

item.ptxt: Initialization when disconnecting/reconnecting the battery terminal (see )

test1.ptxt: Using the Diagnostic Trouble Code Chart or the Problem Symptoms Table, determine which system circuit or part should be inspected.
Following the instructions in step 5, repair the malfunctioning system or part.

After repairs are completed, check that the problem has been eliminated. (If the problem recurs, perform a confirmation test under the same environment and conditions as when the problem first occurred.)
If the problem was one for which a DTC was stored, perform the diagnosis judgment result check.
Restore each setting to the vehicle condition confirmed in step 4.

atten4.ptxt: If there are any items whose settings cannot be restored, be sure to explain to the customer.
